subject: Language B

objectives.name: Get your message across clearly, adjusting how you communicate to the setting and what you want to achieve.
Recognise the language a situation and audience call for, and choose expressions that fit personal exchanges and communication across cultures.
Express your ideas and respond to other people’s ideas with accurate language and a smooth flow.
Select the ideas you need for a topic, arrange them coherently and present them to your audience.
Work out what written, spoken, visual and combined sound-and-image texts convey; examine their choices and reflect on what you understand.

components.name: Individual oral (SL)

criteria.name: Language
criteria.guidance: Accuracy and fluency: grammar, vocabulary, pronunciation and coherence across the whole oral.

criteria.name: Message
criteria.guidance: Ideas that actually engage the stimulus or extract, developed rather than listed.

criteria.name: Interactive skills: communication
criteria.guidance: Move the conversation forward yourself. Answering only what you are asked caps this.

notes: SL: presentation on a visual stimulus tied to a prescribed theme. HL: presentation on an extract from a studied literary work.
Three criteria: Language 12, Message 12, Interactive skills 6 — total 30.
On paper 1, ignoring context, purpose and audience can score zero for message and conceptual understanding even with strong language.
Language acquisition is the exception to IB's general position on spelling and grammar; language-improvement software is not permitted.

The five prescribed themes apply to both SL and HL. The briefs distinguish these from optional recommended topics, which are not presented here as compulsory syllabus content. The first-assessment-2029 replacement is not used for this 2020 record.

The five objectives are paraphrased from two independently hosted matching IB briefs; the matching guide confirms their numbering. Neither brief publishes per-objective weightings, so those ranges remain null.

Both matching first-assessment-2020 briefs explicitly give the same assessment split at SL and HL: external 75% and individual oral 25% (p. 2 assessment table; https://www.didzdvaris.lt/wp-content/uploads/2020/12/lang-b-2018-en.pdf and https://www.purcellmarian.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/lang-b-2018-en.pdf). HL changes the task demands, not these component percentages.
